title: New Winners at the New York City Marathon
summary:
Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the men's race at the New York City Marathon on Sunday in his very first try at the 26.2-mile distance, after a successful career running half-marathons. He pulled away from Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa in the final mile to win in 2:06:01, with Crippa 13 seconds behind and Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho third, edging defending champion Benson Kipruto.

His time was the third fastest in course history, and the top seven finishers all ran among the ten fastest times ever there. He was the first debut winner since Gebre Gebremariam of Ethiopia in 2010, and American Zouhair Talbi finished sixth in the fastest time ever by a U.S. runner.

Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race for the second time, also winning in 2024, pulling away from countrywoman Hellen Obiri in the final 150 meters to win in 2:24:36. American Jessica McClain passed Obiri, a two-time winner, in the final strides for second, six seconds behind, the first U.S. woman in the top three since 2018.

It was the 50th time the race has run through all five boroughs. In 1976 there were just over 2,000 competitors, including only 88 women; on Sunday about 60,000 runners started, nearly half women, from more than 140 countries. The marathon began in 1970 inside Central Park, where runners looped for its first six years.

For the first time in 15 years the course changed slightly at Mile 20, cutting Bronx turns from seven to five and easing street closures. In the wheelchair races, Switzerland's Marcel Hug won the men's race for the eighth time, passing Daniel Romanchuk in the final 100 meters by just over a second, and Catherine Debrunner won the women's race in 1:40:02, the second-fastest time ever.
why_it_matters: Big races show how years of training and a strong finish can pay off, and how one city event can bring together runners from all over the world.
